label: def:schwinger-measure-unit
title: Schwinger proper-time measure and its unit $\varsigma$
html:
The Schwinger proper-time measure with unit \varsigma is the scale-invariant density on the proper-time half-line,

\mu_\varsigma \;=\; \varsigma\,\frac{ds}{s}, \qquad s \in (0, \infty),

where s is the Schwinger proper-time variable of the one-loop determinant and the scalar \varsigma is the Schwinger measure unit. The shape is rigid: a density f satisfying the scale-invariance functional equation f(\lambda s)\,\lambda = f(s) equals f(1)/s, so \mu_\varsigma is the unique scale-invariant choice up to the single scalar \varsigma. Scale invariance is inherited from the conformal invariance of the horizon boundary datum (prop:horizon-conformal-invariance): the loop's ultraviolet end has no preferred proper-time scale.

The canonical unit is \varsigma = 1: in the logarithmic coordinate the measure of one e-fold [s, e\,s] is exactly \varsigma, and with k_B = 1 (entropy in nats, prop:boltzmann-constant) the unit is denominated in nats per proper-time e-fold. Downstream consumers reference this result for the per-loop measure normalization; under the canonical unit and the per-channel \tfrac12 split, the working per-channel coefficient is \tfrac12 \cdot \frac{1}{4\pi} = \frac{1}{8\pi}.

Conjectural backing of canonicity. Defining \mu_1 names a construction; the canonicity of the choice \varsigma = 1 is not proved. It is conditionally forced by the computational-time identification conj:schwinger-measure-computational-time, through the moment identity n \cdot N(n) = n! for the binding normalizer N(n), and, separately, by the framework premises P1 (substrate scale-freedom) and P2 (proper time as computational time) stated there. Unconditionally it remains a unit convention of the same species the framework canonizes elsewhere for discrete time steps. Empirical support is exact rather than numerical: the unit-measure moment identity holds at orders 1 through 6, and a pin-invariance falsifier eliminates every intrinsic per-step rival unit.

Notation. The unit is written \varsigma (varsigma). The archimedean Lean shell writes c for the same scalar; the notation register reserves plain c for color, with c_q and c_k also taken, so this paper uses \varsigma.
